single_story.note: All sources cover the Oct 6, 2026 launch of Mistral Large 4.

the_news.text: On Oct 6, 2026, French AI lab Mistral launched a public preview of Mistral Large 4 ("Le Chonk"), a 1-trillion-parameter model it pitches for cyber defense. Weights are due at the end of October. [CLAIM: Mistral says] it is the best open-weight model from the US or Europe, and an independent index puts it well behind the top closed models.

why_it_matters.text: Mistral is pitching ML4 as an alternative to closed US models that can be withdrawn or that refuse security work, and to Chinese open models. It positions the model as a sovereignty play for Europe.
The independent score (38 vs. 58 for the leader) shows the model is still well short of the frontier. Weights are not yet out, so the "open" label is pending.

facts.text: Mistral released Mistral Large 4 (ML4), nicknamed "Le Chonk", on Tuesday Oct 6, 2026, as a public preview via its API (Mistral Studio), with model weights expected at the end of October.
notes: TechCrunch says weights come "in just three weeks, after safety testing is complete". CNBC says wider release "later this month".

facts.text: ML4 is not yet an open-weight model: weights have not been released, and the preview is accessed through an API (TechCrunch calls it a "public guardrail endpoint"). Artificial Analysis lists it as proprietary until weights ship.
notes: Wired describes it as a "freely available model that can be used and customized by anyone" even though it is only in preview.

facts.text: ML4 is a natively multimodal model with 1 trillion parameters, 49 billion of them active.
notes: Documentation cited by the-decoder.com lists 1.05 trillion total parameters with a fine-grained mixture-of-experts design and a 1.6B-parameter vision encoder.

facts.text: On the independent Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, ML4 scores 38. That is up from 9 for Mistral Large 3 and 14 for Mistral Medium 3.5. It is well below the leader, Claude Opus 5.5 (Max), at 58.
notes: Artificial Analysis says 38 is comparable to GPT-6 Luna (max, 38) and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (max, 39). It calls ML4 the most intelligent model from outside the US and China.
The-decoder.com says the model trails the leading closed models and several Chinese open-weight models.

facts.text: Artificial Analysis gives ML4 a score of 50 on its Cyber Index, level with GLM-5.3-Flash and behind MiMo-V2.6-Pro (56). Its best result is 82% on CyberGym-E2E-AA, ahead of MiMo-V2.6-Pro (79%) and GPT-6 Luna (max, 78%).
notes: Artificial Analysis says ML4 would rank among the top three open-weight models on the Cyber Index once weights are released. Mistral says top five among all models worldwide.
Artificial Analysis does not mention refusals by Claude or GPT in its comparison.

facts.text: Mistral says Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra score near zero on the vulnerability reproduce-and-patch test because they refuse the task. ML4 scores 82% and is the highest of any model.
notes: Single outlet relaying the company's claim. the-decoder.com notes the test measures provider policy as much as model capability. The independent Artificial Analysis post lists the 82% result but compares it only with MiMo-V2.6-Pro and GPT-6 Luna.

facts.text: Mistral says it is red-teaming the model with security firms, vetted partners and government agencies until weights ship. Those groups get a version with reduced moderation and expanded cyber capabilities.
notes: the-decoder.com notes Mistral does not explain how the model reliably tells legitimate vulnerability research from attack prep.
Mistral also says ML4 refuses malicious cyber prompts more than any other open model, and blocks 93.3% of attacks in Lakera's B3 benchmark. This is company-reported only.

facts.text: Mistral's pitch is that closed-model safety filters block legitimate defensive work, attackers jailbreak those models anyway, and losing provider access mid-incident is itself a security risk. ML4 can run in private clouds or on-premise.
notes: Lample (Wired): "what really matters is to own the model".

facts.text: Mistral says it trained ML4 from scratch on its own European compute using Nvidia Grace Blackwell GPUs, and will offer a European variant run fully under European law.
notes: GPU count differs: 3,800 (the-decoder.com) vs 4,000 (TechCrunch, CNBC). CNBC says training took two months.

facts.text: Mistral says ML4 is the best open-weights model from the US or Europe on aggregated benchmarks, and the strongest open-weight model developed outside China by a "substantial margin".
notes: Artificial Analysis says it is the most intelligent model from outside the US and China, which is a related but different claim. It also ranks below several Chinese open-weight models.

facts.text: In coding, ML4 scores 49.8% on the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index, ahead of DeepSeek V4 Pro and Qwen3.8 Max. In a Mistral-run blind evaluation with Surge AI it scored 3.74 of 5, second of five models behind Claude Opus 5 (4.22).
notes: The Surge AI evaluation was run by Mistral. CNBC reports the model "still lags behind the frontier in areas such as coding."

facts.text: During the preview, ML4 costs $0.68 per million input tokens, $2.09 per million output tokens and $0.07 for cached input.
notes: Artificial Analysis lists standard pricing of $1.36/$4.18 with $0.14 cached, and says the first two weeks have a 50% launch discount. The-decoder.com also mentions the doubled rates without explaining the discount.
Artificial Analysis says cost per task is $1.13 at standard pricing and $0.57 with the discount, over 4x similar-intelligence open-weight models (GLM-5.3-Flash $0.25; DeepSeek V4.1 Flash $0.27).

facts.text: Mistral says the reinforcement-learning run behind the preview is still ongoing and it expects significant improvements over the coming weeks.
Mistral plans to publish architecture details, the license and post-training methods with the weights at the end of the month, so the license terms are unknown for now.

background.text: Mistral raised a Series D in September 2026, called the largest ever raise by a European tech company. Sources give it as 3 billion euros (about $3.4B) at a 21 billion euro valuation, or $3.3 billion at $24 billion.
notes: Figures differ by currency conversion. TechCrunch says Samsung led the Series D and ASML led the Series C.

background.text: In June, the Trump administration placed temporary restrictions on the distribution of models from OpenAI and Anthropic over cyberattack concerns. Earlier this year, Hugging Face used Z.ai's GLM 5.2 to defend against a breach after US closed models' guardrails blocked it.
notes: Wired and CNBC each cover one of these events. The Wired description of incidents of US-made models attacking companies is unattributed.

terms.name: Open-weight model
terms.definition: A model whose trained parameters are released so others can modify and self-host it, unlike closed systems from OpenAI and Anthropic.

terms.name: Distillation
terms.definition: Training a smaller model on the outputs of a larger one. The US government has accused Chinese labs of abusing it.

terms.name: Mixture-of-experts
terms.definition: An architecture where only some of the model's parameters (here 49B of about 1T) are active for a given input.

terms.name: Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index
terms.definition: An independent index aggregating ten benchmarks across different domains.

terms.name: Red-teaming
terms.definition: Testing a model for misuse risks. Mistral does this with security firms, vetted partners and government agencies before weights ship.

article_photos.caption: In the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, Mistral Large 4 trails the leading closed models from Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google, as well as several open-weight models from China. ML4 is still listed as proprietary because its weights haven't been released yet.
Mistral Large 4 scores near the top in scientific coding, though GPT-6 Astra and Qwen3.8 still post higher numbers.
On automated business workflows, Mistral Large 4 trails GLM-5.3 slightly but beats Kimi K3 and Deepseek V4 Pro.

not_answered: Primary source not opened: Mistral's own announcement page or blog/documentation. Only its X post was opened, so the benchmark and refusal claims could not be checked against it.

Whether Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra really score near zero on the vulnerability test because they refuse: only Mistral's claim relayed by the-decoder.com, and not confirmed by Artificial Analysis.
How Mistral separates legitimate vulnerability research from attack prep (the-decoder.com says Mistral does not explain).
License terms for the open weights, which are not published yet.
Context window: 1M tokens (the-decoder.com) vs 512k (Artificial Analysis) is unresolved.
GPU count for training: 3,800 vs 4,000 is unresolved.
Whether the preview price of $0.68/$2.09 is the 50% launch discount: Artificial Analysis says yes, the-decoder.com does not say.
No independent expert comment on the cyber claims or on the model's real-world security value. Renda's quote is from July and on Mistral's market position.
